description: COMBINE the current global best (brief 19 HEAD 7d87b96a, ~4860us, which still routes n=4096 to torch.geqrf ~52k us — the LARGEST remaining geomean term) with brief 13's n=4096 cooperative-cluster win (6dfdc0736): brief 13 got n=4096 B=2 to 31448us = 1.66x faster than geqrf via a thread-block cluster of K=16 CTAs (hardware cap) splitting one tall 4096-row panel by rows, cross-CTA reductions via DSMEM/cluster.sync (sm_100a), hybrid (cluster for tall panels m>=256, single-CTA for short), whole-batch TF32 trailing GEMM (loosest budget ~1.2e-2 at n=4096). This n=4096 path is ORTHOGONAL to the n<=2048/tiny-n/TF32-trailing wins in the best and stacks cleanly. Add n=4096 to the best's custom path via brief 13's _blocked_qr_cluster; keep everything else identical. Re-measure min-of-3 (bimodal benchmark). Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

COMBINE parent A (global best 4859.9us, routed n=4096->geqrf ~52k) + parent B's (brief 13) n=4096 cooperative-cluster panel. Added 4096 to _SUPPORTED_N + new _CLUSTER_N; ported panel_factor_cluster_kernel + panel_factor_cluster launcher (sm_100a thread-block cluster K=16 hw-max, DSMEM/cluster.sync cross-CTA reductions) + _blocked_qr_cluster (hybrid: cluster panel for m>=mhyb=256, single-CTA panel for short trailing panels, whole-batch TF32 trailing GEMM). custom_kernel routes n=4096->_blocked_qr_cluster; ALL other n byte-identical to parent A. Integration fix: prime single-CTA SMEM cap for m=mhyb(256) NOT m=n=4096 (the latter requests 262KB > B200 ~228KB opt-in cap => cudaErrorInvalidValue). MEASURED min-of-3 (bimodal): geomean 4657.85us (runs 9900.76/4660.63/4657.85; first was 2x contention) = 1.043x over parent A. n=4096 B=2 shape 52k(geqrf)->31432us (=1.66x, matches parent B 31448). All other shapes match parent A exactly (n=512 8730us, n=32 32.86us). Profile: panel_factor_cluster_kernel 66.5% of n=4096 time, TF32 cutlass trailing ~22%, single-CTA short-panel 2.5%. Validates CLEAN: all 22 tests (incl n=4096 dense+upper) + invariance + diff_correctness + offgrid guards.

Optional brief direction: route n=2048 B=8 through the cooperative cluster too (added 2048 to _CLUSTER_N; K=16, mhyb=256, whole-batch TF32 trailing -- same precision parent A used for n=2048). Parent A's single-CTA panel ran only 8 CTAs on 148 SMs at B=8 (under-occupied like n=4096 B=2 but milder); 8*16=128 cluster CTAs nearly fill the 148 SMs. MEASURED min-of-3 (very stable, all 3 runs within 0.001%): geomean 4595.23us (runs 4595.23/4595.29/4595.25) = 1.0136x over trial 1 (4657.85), 1.0576x over parent A (4859.9). n=2048 B=8 shape 19197us(single-CTA)->16295us = 1.18x on that shape. n=4096 unchanged 31432us; all other shapes match parent A. Validates CLEAN: all 22 tests (incl n=2048 dense factor_resid 0.867 / rankdef 3.45 / mixed 0.817, all well within 20*n*eps budget) + invariance + diff_correctness + offgrid guards.

Swept K for the n=2048 B=8 cluster (clean runs on shape5): K=4->16865, K=6->~37k(maps poorly,8*6=48), K=8->15208, K=12->16148, K=16->16295us. K=8 is the optimum (8*8=64 CTAs; fewer cluster ranks => cheaper per-column cluster.sync than K=16 while still covering enough SMs at B=8). Locked n=2048->K=8, n=4096 stays K=16. MEASURED min-of-3 (clean,stable): geomean 4567.02us (runs 4571.98/4568.51/4567.02) = 1.0062x over trial 2 (K=16, 4595.23), 1.0641x over parent A (4859.9). n=2048 B=8 shape ~15219us. Profile (n=2048): panel_factor_cluster_kernel 61.1% of time, single-CTA short-panel<512> 5.3%, TF32 cutlass trailing the rest -- cluster is the dominant, latency/sync-bound cost (same character as n=4096). Validates CLEAN: all 22 tests + invariance + diff_correctness + offgrid guards.

Tested cluster threads 256->512 (launch_bounds 256,4 -> 512,2): the brief/parent-B note said more threads/CTA could hide the cluster.sync stalls (kernel is 6.25% occupancy at n=4096). REGRESSION on the clean run: shape5 n=2048 15219->16168us, shape6 n=4096 31432->35064us, geomean min-of-3 4634.35us (clean run; other 2 were contention) vs trial 3 4567.02us. The wider 512-thread CTA at only 2 blocks/SM (vs 256-thread/4-blocks) loses more CTA-level latency-hiding parallelism than the extra warps-per-scheduler buys. 256 threads / 4 blocks-per-SM remains best. Validates CLEAN (22 tests + 3 guards). Reverting threads to 256 for the next direction.

KEEPER: locked the best config after the thread (trial 4) and mhyb sweeps. Reverted to 256 threads / launch_bounds(256,4) (512 regressed) and mhyb=256 (swept: 128->shape5 15328/shape6 31586, 256->15219/31432 best, 512 regresses hard forcing tall panels onto single-CTA). Source byte-identical to trial 3 + sweep findings recorded in comments. FINAL config: n=4096 -> cluster K=16 / n=2048 -> cluster K=8, both mhyb=256 / 256 threads / whole-batch TF32 trailing; all n<=1024, tiny-n, off-grid EXACTLY as parent A. geomean min-of-3 clean 4588.99us (runs 14133 contention/4594.32/4588.99; equals ~4567 on faster-clock runs, both within the ~1% clean-mode jitter) = ~1.06x over parent A (4859.9). n=4096 B=2 31456us (1.66x over geqrf 52k, matches parent B 31448); n=2048 B=8 15240us (1.26x over parent A single-CTA 19197). Profile (n=4096): panel_factor_cluster_kernel 66.5%, TF32 cutlass trailing ~22%, single-CTA short-panel 2.5% -- cluster is the latency/sync-bound bottleneck. Validates CLEAN: all 22 tests + invariance + diff_correctness + offgrid guards.

COMBINE landed and STACKED CLEANLY, then extended past the brief. Best committed: trial 2 (8f4c188f) geomean 4567.024us = 1.064x over parent A (4859.9); equivalent keeper trial 4 (25941e9f) measured 4588.99 on a slower-clock clean run (same source config, pure clean-mode GPU-clock jitter, both within ~1%). Progression: basic combine (n=4096 cluster, 4657.85) -> +n=2048 cluster K=16 (4595.23) -> n=2048 K=8 (4567.02). All n<=1024 / tiny-n / off-grid kept BYTE-IDENTICAL to parent A; only the two low-batch large-n shapes changed. WHAT EACH EDIT DID: (1) ported parent B's panel_factor_cluster_kernel + launcher + _blocked_qr_cluster onto parent A; integration fix = prime the single-CTA SMEM cap for m=mhyb(256) not m=n=4096 (262KB>228KB cap=cudaErrorInvalidValue). n=4096 B=2 52k(geqrf)->31456us=1.66x (matches parent B exactly). (2) the OPTIONAL brief direction PAID OFF: routing n=2048 B=8 onto the cluster too (it ran only 8 single-CTA CTAs on 148 SMs) dropped that shape 19197->15240us=1.26x. (3) K SWEEP confirmed n=2048 wants K=8 not 16 (K=4->16865,K=6->~37k,K=8->15208,K=12->16148,K=16->16295) -- LOWER K at HIGHER batch, as the brief hypothesized. (4) mhyb=256 best (128 slightly worse, 512 regresses). (5) cluster threads 256->512 REGRESSED (4567->4634). All 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN every trial. Profile: panel_factor_cluster_kernel is 66.5% of n=4096 / 61.1% of n=2048 time and is latency/sync-bound (parent B noted 6.25% occupancy, 1 active warp/scheduler at B=2). OPEN DIRECTIONS still unexplored under this objective: (a) the cluster kernel's per-column 3x cluster.sync chain over cb columns is the bottleneck -- a 2-LEVEL cluster panel (micro-panel block-WY apply like parent A's single-CTA 2-level kernel, cutting the serial sync count) could attack the sync-bound stall directly; (b) the trailing-update TF32 GEMM at n=4096 is ~22% and is launched per-panel as many small cutlass tiles (482 instances) -- fusing or batching those, or a wider cb just for the trailing while keeping cb=16 for the panel, is untested; (c) n=4096 K could be swept like n=2048 was (only K=16 tested here, inherited from parent B; a 2-level cluster might prefer different K); (d) mhyb was swept at the shared {128,256,512} granularity only -- a per-n mhyb (e.g. 384) between the tested points is unprobed; (e) the n=4096 single-CTA short-panel tail (m<256, 2.5%) still uses threads=512 -- untuned. The basic combine win is real and above noise; the manager should consider both pushing the cluster kernel structurally (a) and whether the n=2048-on-cluster win generalizes to a future n=1024/B=60 case.
